title: HETU in Context
description: Start with the project overview to understand HETU as a local-first GATE preparation system built around structured PYQ analysis, spaced re-attempts, readiness signals, and focused buddy study. The document also establishes the account-isolation and deployment assumptions that explain many of the architectural choices in later steps.

title: Application Bootstrap
description: The browser entry point mounts the React client and coordinates PWA behavior, while the root application shell initializes authentication and preferences before routing begins. Reading the router alongside them reveals how public, authenticated, lazy-loaded, and failure-recovery paths compose the runtime introduced in Step 1.
languageLesson: React applications often separate the DOM bootstrap, long-lived providers, and route tree so initialization policy can evolve independently from page-level features. Lazy route imports reduce the initial bundle, while an error boundary provides a controlled recovery path for stale deployment chunks.

title: Responsive Application Shell
description: Building on the route tree, the shared shell surrounds every study page with desktop or mobile navigation, synchronization status, contextual coaching, and global controls. The global stylesheet supplies the design tokens, safe-area rules, motion, and print behavior that let the same interface feel coherent on the web and inside the native Android host.

title: Local-First Foundation
description: Under the shell, Dexie is the primary offline data store and the synchronization engine moves tracked writes to Supabase in dependency order while preserving pending local changes during conflicts. Shared database contracts and authentication state keep every persisted row user-scoped, making the isolation promises from Step 1 concrete rather than merely a UI convention.
languageLesson: TypeScript contracts can model compatibility by requiring fields for new writes while permitting older persisted rows to omit newly introduced properties. That distinction is essential for evolving local-first schemas without making existing offline data unreadable.

title: Core Study Lifecycle
description: With persistence established, the active-session page runs the timed solve-and-tag loop and records structured evidence about outcomes, patterns, triggers, and causes. Logging and review then turn that evidence into durable journal records and scheduled work, providing the general lifecycle that specialized PYQ practice reuses in the following steps.

title: Audited PYQ Catalog
description: The PYQ catalog is generated rather than maintained as ad hoc UI data: an allowlisted builder admits five GATE-level books, localizes assets, and locks exact question and answer-key expectations. Classification and audit passes preserve the question identity set while enforcing stable subjects, topics, provenance, and per-book aggregates before the runtime can consume the bank.

title: PYQ Test Contract
description: The PYQ page projects the audited catalog from Step 6 into the established timed test interface, adding book-aware selection without changing answer submission, analysis, or session-resume behavior. The session module makes every commit an immutable receipt containing the question snapshot, selected answer, timing, session identity, and book identity, so journal entries and resumed sets cannot drift when the bank evolves.
languageLesson: Immutable receipt objects are an event-sourcing pattern: capture the facts required to explain a decision at write time instead of looking them up from mutable reference data later. Deterministic identifiers then make retries safe and prevent duplicate commits.

title: Spaced Re-attempt Loop
description: Attempt receipts from Step 7 feed an offline-compatible D3–D10–D30 ladder that selects due work, evaluates fresh answers, and advances or reschedules the learner. The dedicated re-attempt page restores both ordinary logged questions and PYQ snapshots into the same test semantics, preserving locked answers, skipped-question navigation, timers, and second-attempt history.

title: Readiness and Planning
description: The evidence accumulated by sessions, PYQs, and re-attempts becomes higher-level guidance through readiness scoring, long-running weakness snapshots, and planner execution. The dashboard presents those calculations as prioritized next actions, closing the learner-facing loop from solving a question to deciding what to study next.

title: Database Integrity Boundary
description: The PostgreSQL migrations mirror the local-first model with user-owned study data, row-level security, immutable PYQ attempt history, durable session state, and guarded audit metadata. These database constraints are the server-side enforcement behind the client contracts from Steps 4 and 7, so malformed or cross-user writes remain invalid even if they bypass the interface.
languageLesson: PostgreSQL row-level security applies ownership rules inside the database, while triggers and constraints protect invariants such as immutable answer receipts. Together they create a trust boundary that does not depend on every client behaving correctly.

title: Buddy and Edge Services
description: Beyond individual study, the Buddy workspace adds realtime presence, focused chat, shared question references, and relationship workflows on top of the same authenticated data boundary. Supabase Edge Functions process transactional notification jobs and scheduled study reminders, keeping privileged tokens and delivery logic outside the browser client.

title: Android Native Delivery
description: The Capacitor activity hosts the web application and safely maps supported app links back into its route model, while Android notification services and workers provide authenticated actions and reliable inline replies. The Android release guide connects this native runtime to signing, Firebase push setup, device verification, app links, and performance budgets.
languageLesson: Android WorkManager is suited to network-bound notification actions because it persists queued work, applies connectivity constraints, and exposes retry-aware completion results even when the app process is no longer active.

title: Verification and Operations
description: The final stop shows how HETU protects the full story: focused tests exercise book-aware PYQ commits, immutable snapshots, legacy restoration, navigation, and re-attempt behavior rather than checking isolated rendering alone. Package workflows define the repeatable content and quality gates, while the deployment runbook covers Supabase, edge functions, Vercel, smoke tests, operations, and rollback.
